statement: On a fixed set of structural features, short Indus inscriptions agree more closely with Aramaic and Hebrew inscriptions than with control inscriptions from non-Semitic languages. Agreement is measured as distance between feature profiles, with object family and text length held fixed.
why_structure_only: No sign-to-sound values are assumed. Each script's signs are treated as units; only repetition, position and diversity are compared. No word-level reading is claimed.

corpora.target_1: Indus Mohenjo-daro and Harappa seal inscriptions, from ICIT is NOT allowed (metadata only, amendment item 4). Use a licensed published source only: Mackay or Marshall plates, or Mukhopadhyay 2023 CC BY 4.0 figures, to be decided before any reading.
corpora.comparison_A: Aramaic inscriptions (seals, ostraca, short dedications). Source and licence to be recorded in source_log.csv before any text is read.
corpora.comparison_B: Hebrew inscriptions (seals, ostraca, short dedications). Source and licence to be recorded in source_log.csv before any text is read.
corpora.control_C: Non-Semitic short inscriptions, e.g. Old Tamil or Prakrit, from sources with a checked licence. At least one control is required.
corpora.rule: No corpus is read until its licence is logged. If a corpus has no licence, it is excluded and the exclusion is recorded.

features: F1: share of texts whose first unit repeats elsewhere in the same text
F2: share of texts whose last unit repeats elsewhere in the same text
F3: unigram entropy per text, binned by text length
F4: proportion of units that appear in more than one text (cross-text recurrence)
statistic: For each corpus, the mean of F1-F4 over texts of length 3-8 units. Distance from Indus to each comparison corpus is the sum of absolute feature differences. Test: Indus-to-Aramaic and Indus-to-Hebrew distances both smaller than Indus-to-control distance.
null: Length-matched random sequences drawn from each corpus's own unit inventory, and within-text shuffles. Repeat 10,000 times to get the null distribution of distances.
falsifier: Indus is not closer to both Aramaic and Hebrew than to the non-Semitic control on at least three of four features, or the result disappears under the length-matched null.
controls: Length fixed to 3-8 units. Object family (seal vs ostracon vs dedication) fixed within each comparison, or reported as a genre effect if it is not. Report every feature result, including failures.
status: Written and hashed before any comparison corpus is read. Results will go in results/structure_semitic_P20_2026-11-07.md. Single reader (Claude). Exploratory until a second reader and a licensed corpus are in place.
